title: NEMT & Medical Courier Dispatch Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: A Field-Tested Operating Workbook for Launching a Medical Courier Business, Landing Direct Contracts, Working Hiring Fleets and Specialized Lanes, Pricing Routes for Real Profit, and Building the Entity, Insurance, and Enrollment Foundation

worksheets.title: Launch Sequence and Direct Contract Pipeline
worksheets.purpose: Sequence the launch of a medical courier operation so that no money goes into vehicles, insurance, or entity paperwork before a contract justifies it, then build a direct-contract pipeline that replaces middleman pay with lab, pharmacy, and clinic clients who pay the full rate and sign terms that protect the operator.
instructions: Start with the vehicle you already own and record it before considering any purchase; a van or Sprinter only enters the plan when a signed contract covers its payment.
Fill in the rate benchmarks before you contact a single prospect, so every offer is judged against third-party day rates, vehicle-class ladders, and the per-stop spread large companies keep.
Block a fixed daily window for applications and calls, and log every submission with the date, contact name, follow-up call time, and the response you received.
Write the client's stated volume, hours, and stop count into each bid in plain language, and attach your cancellation and subcontractor terms before anything is signed.
Review this sheet weekly; move any route that clashes with your day job into the decline or backup-coverage column instead of stretching your availability.

fields.name: launch_level_and_vehicle
fields.prompt: Identify which courier level you are starting at and which vehicle you already own. Explain why you will launch with that vehicle instead of buying a van or Sprinter, and name the signed contract that would justify any upgrade.
fields.example: I start at level one in the paid-off sedan I already drive. Medical Courier Connection says no van or Sprinter purchase until a signed contract covers the payment [Medical Courier Connection — o1VRiVMJTpY @ 00:24:07]. Sarah Davis adds that a bigger vehicle expands capacity but does not automatically raise your level [Sarah Davis | The D&G Way — bzwpVnDnULQ @ 00:02:47].

fields.name: paperwork_order
fields.prompt: Decide your paperwork order for the first ninety days. State whether you will form an LLC, pull an EIN, and open business banking before your first contract, or start under your name and SSN as a 1099 contractor, and explain why.
fields.example: Miles & Money and Diamond Hunter Enterprises push LLC, EIN and business banking first, while Sarah Davis says levels one and two needed a name, SSN and 1099 status. I will start as a 1099 contractor, then form the LLC once a vendor posting demands it, keeping overhead low [STICK WITH US DELIVERY 🚚 📦 — cWa2fFpFFFU @ 00:05:40].

fields.name: training_and_insurance_stack
fields.prompt: List the HIPAA and bloodborne pathogen certificates you hold or will complete, and the exact insurance you will carry. Note whether a client has told you its required liability limit before you pay any premium, and record that limit.
fields.example: Diamond Hunter Enterprises says commercial auto plus business liability is needed even solo [Diamond Hunter Enterprises — zQaL3OdQ2D8 @ 00:04:29], but Tony of Stick With Us Delivery says to ask whether the company requires $300,000 or $1 million first [STICK WITH US DELIVERY 🚚 📦 — gvxg69CITsE @ 00:04:22]. I hold both certificates and will bind only the limit requested.

fields.name: market_rate_benchmarks
fields.prompt: Write down the rate benchmarks you will measure every offer against, by vehicle class and by payer type. Compare third-party day rates with direct-contract pricing and note the spread large courier companies keep between driver pay and client billing.
fields.example: LearnCargo puts third-party medical courier work near $200 per day [LearnCargo — TkA2pcOAGoQ @ 00:01:58]. JT Automations ladders sedans at $800 to $1,500 weekly up to $4,000 to $8,000 in a non-CDL box truck [JT Automations — gpeFpvbyWg4 @ 00:04:02]. Giganomic Era shows drivers earning $10 per stop while clients pay $20 to $50 [Giganomic Era — YewfRfz9eUI @ 00:01:26].

fields.name: cash_reserve_plan
fields.prompt: Calculate three months of operating expenses, including fuel, insurance, phone, and maintenance, and state where that reserve sits today. Explain how you will cover the gap if a direct client takes ninety days to send the first check.
fields.example: I will not accept invoice-paid direct clients until three full months of operating expenses sit in a separate account. Ken and Linda of Medical Courier Connection set that rule because billing cycles run 20 to 30 days and first checks can take 90 days to arrive [Medical Courier Connection — o1VRiVMJTpY @ 00:14:00].

fields.name: prospecting_script_and_schedule
fields.prompt: Write the opening line you will use on prospecting calls and the exact time windows you will dial. Name the departments you will call directly, the decision-makers you will ask for, and how you will cluster in-person visits geographically.
fields.example: Lunch-break calls open with 'Are your deliveries currently handled internally...?' [Giganomic Era — 7Mz5ctFZBX0 @ 00:05:23]. I dial direct department lines, never the main hospital number, between 9:00 and 11:00 a.m. on Tuesday or Wednesday [Giganomic Era — jv40GZPfRSc @ 00:01:44], asking lab directors and pharmacy managers by name, then visit clinics in one cluster per afternoon.

fields.name: application_cadence
fields.prompt: Set your daily application target and your follow-up rule for every submission. List the job boards and keyword alerts you will monitor, and describe how you will keep applying after the first contract lands instead of stopping.
fields.example: Leelah committed to 25 applications daily, landed a first contract around day seven, then pushed to 40 to 50 per day [Leelah The Entrepreneur — UUrhf6VurIA @ 00:05:24]. I will match that on Indeed, CB Driver and Google alerts, and call the same day after each submission, leaving professional voicemails [My Business Vibe 9 — mm9doNupm1k @ 00:04:18].

fields.name: direct_pricing_terms
fields.prompt: Draft the pricing terms you will propose to your first direct client. Include a per-pickup minimum or weekly retainer, plus your terms for weekend work, holiday coverage, after-hour requests, emergency STAT service, and waiting time, and explain which term you expect to matter most.
fields.example: Giganomic Era charges a $35 minimum per pickup or a $750 to $1,000 weekly retainer and says the bigger opportunity is negotiating weekend work, holiday coverage, after-hour requests, emergency STAT service and waiting time [Giganomic Era — YV5-h4wgh4Q @ 00:03:58]. A comparable direct oxygen route paid $2,620 monthly, about $131 per day [Giganomic Era — YV5-h4wgh4Q @ 00:05:08].

fields.name: contract_protection_clauses
fields.prompt: List the protective clauses you will write into every bid and contract. Cover how you record the client's stated volume assumptions, what cancellation language you require, and which subcontractor or approval clauses you must review before hiring a driver.
fields.example: Medical Courier Connection writes the client's stated assumptions into the bid so misrepresented volume is on paper [Medical Courier Connection — o1VRiVMJTpY @ 00:36:30], and pay-the-remainder cancellation language forced a bank client to pay out about 8 months [Medical Courier Connection — o1VRiVMJTpY @ 00:27:30]. I will hire only when $300 to $500 weekly remains after driver pay.

fields.name: availability_and_capacity_rule
fields.prompt: Map your day-job hours against every route you are considering, including morning and evening runs. State which routes you will decline, where you will offer backup or overflow coverage instead, and how you will avoid overpromising around-the-clock availability.
fields.example: My day job runs midday, so I keep early morning and evening routes and decline anything that clashes, offering backup and overflow coverage instead of 24/7 promises [Giganomic Era — 7Mz5ctFZBX0 @ 00:06:20]. Giganomic Era puts it plainly: a missed opportunity is better than a failed contract that damages your reputation [Giganomic Era — 7Mz5ctFZBX0 @ 00:06:36].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 1 is complete when the launch vehicle is one you already own, three months of operating expenses are banked or scheduled, the liability limit is confirmed by a client before purchase, at least 25 daily applications are logged with same-day follow-up, and every bid carries written volume assumptions and cancellation language.

worksheets.title: Hiring Fleets, App Strategy, and Specialized Lanes
worksheets.purpose: Choose which hiring fleets, brokerages, and apps deserve your onboarding hours, set the insurance limits and credentials that act as the entry moat, and decide which specialized lane, STAT, cold chain, specimens, or organs, you can safely enter with the certifications, coolers, and relationships already in hand.
instructions: List every target company with your vehicle class, its published pay floor or weekly cap, and whether it has confirmed routes in your exact market.
Complete each application in full on the first pass, check every availability day, then call the listed dispatch number rather than waiting for an email.
Disclose your full background truthfully on every vetting form, and note any credential, such as a TWIC card, that could move you to the front of the line.
Before accepting a specialized lane, confirm the certifications, damage insurance, cooler count, and dry ice limits it requires, and write each one down.
Run the STAT checklist on every stacked request, and record each decline with the reason so your patterns become visible over a month of routes.

fields.name: vehicle_class_pay_floor
fields.prompt: Record the daily pay floor that applies to your vehicle class and the weekly caps published by any fleet you are targeting. Explain how a vehicle upgrade would change your ceiling and which signed work would have to come first.
fields.example: Diamond Hunter Enterprises sets a $200 daily sedan minimum, $400 to $500 for a cargo van or Sprinter, and $800 to $1,200 for a box truck [Diamond Hunter Enterprises — kDbf0ylOUNw @ 00:01:00]. American Expediting caps cars at $1,200 weekly, vans at $1,500 and box trucks near $2,000 [Eann — tidUl8-lql8 @ 00:02:10]. My sedan floor is $200.

fields.name: application_completeness
fields.prompt: Describe how you will complete every fleet application in full on the first attempt. Note which availability days you will check, which dispatch numbers you will call instead of waiting, and how often you will follow up by name.
fields.example: Giganomic Era warns companies only contact applicants who complete the full form [Giganomic Era — VOBDHU3FYtA @ 00:05:53]. On Strategic Delivery Solutions forms I check Sunday through Saturday because the goal is a callback, then call the listed number [Side Hustle 247 — WVwEyiww470 @ 00:04:40]. I call dispatch by name every five to seven days.

fields.name: market_route_check
fields.prompt: Before investing onboarding hours, confirm whether each target company actually has routes in your exact market. List the companies, the date you asked, the answer you received, and what silence from a company will mean for your next move.
fields.example: Giganomic Era says silence usually means no routes exist in that market, so confirm before onboarding [Giganomic Era — 7k3sVGSbmRA @ 00:04:03]. Applicants without courier experience still get turned down when the vehicle fails age requirements or insurance limits run too low [Giganomic Era — 7k3sVGSbmRA @ 00:05:11]. I ask about local routes, vehicle age and limits on the first call.

fields.name: insurance_agent_script
fields.prompt: Write the script you will use with your insurance agent when raising limits for paid delivery. Describe the work you pursue, the per-person, per-accident, and property damage limits you request, and whether you need an endorsement or commercial policy.
fields.example: Following Giganomic Era, I tell the agent I am pursuing pharmacy, medical supply and local business delivery, ask for 100,000 per person, 300,000 per accident and 50,000 or 100,000 property damage, and confirm whether paid delivery needs an endorsement or a commercial policy [Giganomic Era — FzfSZhrc8rM @ 00:08:02]. Those 100/300 limits act as the entry moat.

fields.name: app_vs_contract_strategy
fields.prompt: Decide what role delivery apps will play in your schedule, if any. State whether you will refuse apps, use them as gap fillers, or run them alongside contracted routes, and explain how apps differ from a recurring customer.
fields.example: Lavish Life refuses apps entirely, while Giganomic Era reports $1,000 to $1,500 weeks on Dispatch and rates Roadie a high-odds gap filler. Giganomic Era also warns gig apps were designed for you to be available, not to win [Giganomic Era — VOBDHU3FYtA @ 00:07:20], and platform access is not a regular customer [Giganomic Era — FzfSZhrc8rM @ 00:09:20].

fields.name: unposted_work_and_credentials
fields.prompt: List the unposted work you will ask each fleet about, such as one-off STAT orders, and the credentials that move you up the line. Note any background issues that could block a credential and how you will disclose them truthfully.
fields.example: Kae says pharmacy fleets posting $15 to $18 hourly routes hand out stat orders paying $80 to $100 [Boss up with Kae — rwv6d5iSQQY @ 00:06:04]. A TWIC card opens Fort Industries aviation pickups [Boss up with Kae — 6vnVGK7rSFQ @ 00:04:37], and one student lost a federal contract over an untruthful UAR disclosure [Diamond Hunter Enterprises — rPBtFcgIPmQ @ 00:02:15].

fields.name: specialized_lane_choice
fields.prompt: Choose which specialized lane you will pursue first: STAT, cold chain, specimens, or organs. List the certifications already in hand, the insurance that would cover damages, and the facility relationship you need before chasing that lane. Explain why that lane fits your vehicle.
fields.example: LearnCargo warns against chasing cold chain or organ contracts without damage insurance and certifications in hand [LearnCargo — 703O5MjUp9A @ 00:04:16], and notes $1,500 to $5,000 weeks belong to couriers with years of hospital or clinic relationships [LearnCargo — 703O5MjUp9A @ 00:03:58]. I start with specimens, holding HIPAA and OSHA bloodborne pathogen training.

fields.name: certification_stack
fields.prompt: Build your certification stack and budget. Decide whether you will stop at the two-certificate minimum or pursue a larger stack, list each course, its cost, and completion date, and note which higher-paying lanes each credential unlocks for your market.
fields.example: Markie Williams calls HIPAA and OSHA bloodborne pathogen training the two most important [Markie Williams Online Certification Courses — WizhPVJ0zVE @ 00:01:13]. A $90 pack adds hazard communication, fire safety, specimen transport, cybersecurity and harassment prevention [HIPAA Training — zLJq8PlUMDQ @ 00:01:10]. Diamond Hunter ties radiopharmaceutical, chemo and Cairo Fertility credentials to $1,500-plus daily [Diamond Hunter Enterprises — jyu_AIm5pAw @ 00:05:35].

fields.name: cooler_and_supply_setup
fields.prompt: Specify your specimen cooler and supply bag setup. Record daily specimen volume and frozen specimen needs from each client, the number of coolers required, your spill kit contents, and the dry ice limit you will enforce in your vehicle.
fields.example: I ask each lab about daily volume and frozen specimens before buying coolers, since some routes run 50 coolers [Medical Courier Connection — oF-_Ka8kNzk @ 00:02:51]. Coolers stay leak proof, puncture resistant and biohazard marked, stocked with a spill kit, baggies, gloves and alcohol-based rubs. I cap dry ice and keep fresh air moving [Medical Courier Connection — oF-_Ka8kNzk @ 00:03:19].

fields.name: stat_stacking_rule
fields.prompt: Write your STAT stacking rule. For each STAT offer, answer where it takes you, the added miles, the added time, and whether it breaks an existing commitment, then state how you will prioritize when two STAT requests collide.
fields.example: Before any stack I check destination, added miles, added time and existing commitments, and decline anything that makes me late [Medical Courier Connection — qLWRmpKkEP0 @ 00:05:10]. A $50 STAT isn't necessarily a $50 opportunity once deadhead counts [Medical Courier Connection — qLWRmpKkEP0 @ 00:02:15]. When two collide, the patient-care specimen runs first [Medical Courier Connection — qLWRmpKkEP0 @ 00:06:15].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 2 is complete when every target company has a confirmed local route answer, your insurance limits meet 100/300 or the specific contract requirement, your certification stack lists dates and costs, your cooler plan matches client specimen volume, and a written STAT rule governs every stacked run.

worksheets.title: Route Pricing, Pay Reality, and the Legal Foundation
worksheets.purpose: Price routes from the ground up instead of accepting advertised pay, net out every deduction and cost before celebrating gross revenue, and lay the entity, insurance, enrollment, and billing foundation that keeps courier and NEMT work legally protected and actually paid.
instructions: Price at least one route with the flat-rate build before quoting any client: time, mileage, markup, and a clean rounded figure.
Gather miles, hours, stops, and daily volume for every offer, and compute effective hourly pay after fuel and weekly carrier deductions.
Mark up every draft contract for exclusivity, specimen liability, termination notice, subcontractor rights, and fuel surcharge language before you sign.
Describe your operation to insurance agents in precise cargo terms, and confirm which coverages, including errors and omissions, each client contract demands.
If NEMT is part of the plan, treat Medicaid enrollment, state transportation registration, and broker credentialing as separate doors, each requiring written confirmation.

fields.name: flat_rate_build
fields.prompt: Build a flat daily rate for one real or prospective route. Record the hours, total miles, your mileage rate, your hourly time value, the subtotal, your markup percentage, and the clean rounded number you will actually quote.
fields.example: Using Giganomic Era's build for a 2.5-hour, 45-mile morning lab route: mileage at 70 cents is $31.50, time at $40 an hour is $100, for $131.50 total. A 25% markup brings it to $164, rounded up to a clean $175 per service day [Giganomic Era — EgbN0cCrzpk @ 00:01:40]. Stat runs are quoted separately at $65-plus.

fields.name: true_route_comparison
fields.prompt: Compare two routes you have been offered using miles, hours, stops, and daily volume rather than advertised pay. Calculate effective pay per hour after fuel for each, and explain which route you will take and why the numbers support it.
fields.example: Sarah Davis shows a $350 route at 250 miles and 10 to 12 hours can lose to a $250 route at 80 miles and 4 hours [Sarah Davis | The D&G Way — hxoZsGym9DU @ 00:08:18]. Samuel B. adds that $40 an hour minus $8 of gas is really $32 [Samuel B. — X99grw6uMuY @ 00:03:30]. I take the shorter route.

fields.name: settlement_deductions
fields.prompt: List every deduction a carrier contract takes from your weekly settlement before you drive a single mile. Total them, subtract them from expected gross, and note the cash buffer you hold for gas, food, and maintenance until settlements start.
fields.example: Dean Medical Courier Academy lists $6.30 administrative, $5 tech data, $15.85 occupational accidental, $4.65 cargo and $25 commercial auto liability, roughly $50 weekly [Dean Medical Courier Academy — q25UyvVRKew @ 00:03:50]. Gilsar Vergara holds a buffer for gas and food until settlements pay and budgets oil changes as often as every two weeks [Gilsar Vergara — _1Xl9_H-PX8 @ 00:04:23].

fields.name: pay_claim_reality_check
fields.prompt: Test the biggest weekly pay claim you have seen against real invoices and route results. Note the conditions behind the claim, any cancellations that cut pay, and the realistic part-time or full-time daily figure you will plan your budget around.
fields.example: Dean Medical Courier Academy's $3,500 weeks came only during driver shortages and bad weather. Dj Mo's real invoice week totaled $891.60 [Dj Mo — Wc0Dykqpw-Q @ 00:05:59]. Pedro Santiago ran 14 stops with one cancellation and made $140 [Pedro “Mr.BetonYou” Santiago — BhO0ZqkVHFk @ 00:11:29]. I budget around a $220 to $230 part-time day [Side Hustle 247 — NjZBEatuBlc @ 00:04:58].

fields.name: contract_red_lines
fields.prompt: Write the contract red lines you will strike or negotiate before signing any carrier or direct agreement. Cover exclusivity, liability caps on specimens, termination notice, subcontractor rights, and fuel surcharge language, and state the minimum terms you will accept.
fields.example: Giganomic Era strikes exclusive service clauses, uncapped specimen liability and no-notice termination, pushing for 30 days notice minimum [Giganomic Era — EgbN0cCrzpk @ 00:06:19]. Dj Mo only takes carrier contracts that allow subcontractors [Dj Mo — twmmoYWAs5Y @ 00:08:07], and Kae asks for a fuel surcharge that rises when gas climbs above $4 [Boss up with Kae — 6vnVGK7rSFQ @ 00:09:32].

fields.name: business_model_and_entity
fields.prompt: Choose your business model, medical courier or NEMT, and your entity structure, LLC or sole proprietorship. Explain the liability exposure that drives the choice and list the formation steps, including EIN and any Type 2 NPI, in the order you will file them.
fields.example: Alton Arell ran six figures without an LLC, while The Couvent Collective calls sole proprietorship a trap. Business Assurance says an LLC protects personal assets [Business Assurance — -U66kxsJM0o @ 00:03:54]. I form the LLC, pull the EIN, then register one Type 2 NPI, since one NPI follows you everywhere [RouteGenie — 3Z74zrMSRtA @ 00:05:37].

fields.name: insurance_description_and_coverage
fields.prompt: Write how you will describe your operation to an insurance agent and list every coverage you will bind. Specify cargo type, radius, and passenger status, and note whether you need errors and omissions or hired and non-owned coverage.
fields.example: I never say 'medical transportation' for sealed specimens, because the agent hears passengers; I spell out cargo, radius and no passengers [Giganomic Era — wJcNFJjkNwA @ 00:03:53]. Medical Courier Connection buys errors and omissions before the lab asks and uses it as a sales tool [Medical Courier Connection — 0eV-OzFHmX8 @ 00:27:25], since cargo coverage protects nothing on a ruined biopsy.

fields.name: enrollment_layers
fields.prompt: If NEMT is in your plan, map every enrollment layer you must clear before billing a trip. List state Medicaid enrollment, state transportation authority registration, broker credentialing, and portal fees, with the written confirmation you will require for each.
fields.example: Nemiton calls enrollment three separate layers; in California, operating without CPUC registration earned a cease and desist after 3 months [Nemiton — qijT2a0o9VE @ 00:01:10]. Motivational Charles paid $631 for NC Tracks access [Motivational Charles — pFLQ24hu-Ac @ 00:00:35]. Geoff Cole says running trips before written Medicaid confirmation means never getting paid [Geoff Cole — dLgmDQavyEU @ 00:00:31].

fields.name: dead_zone_budget
fields.prompt: Budget the enrollment dead zone between applying and approval. Record your startup cost estimate by vehicle type, the number of days you expect to wait, and the operating cash that will carry fuel, insurance, and payroll until the first payment.
fields.example: Geoff Cole prices a single ambulatory van at $15,000 to $30,000 all in, and $30,000 to $50,000 for wheelchair-accessible [Geoff Cole — dLgmDQavyEU @ 00:05:52]. The full process takes 60 to 120 days, a dead zone where you cannot bill Medicaid [Geoff Cole — dLgmDQavyEU @ 00:05:01]. Commercial auto runs $6,000 to $10,000 yearly [Medical Courier Connection — 0eV-OzFHmX8 @ 00:05:40].

fields.name: document_folder_and_billing_readiness
fields.prompt: Assemble your full document folder before submitting any application, and confirm billing readiness before the first trip. List each document, the date you checked names, addresses, and numbers for exact matches, and every state or broker billing submission window.
fields.example: Nemiton builds the entire folder first and checks every name, address and number for exact matches, since one afternoon of checking saves a month of waiting [Nemiton — qijT2a0o9VE @ 00:03:44]. MJ Business Academy warns 50 to 100 unbilled trips pile up fast, so billing software and submission windows are set before launch [MJ Business Academy — OH1QaUPvJ8k @ 00:06:57].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 3 is complete when at least one route carries a documented flat-rate build, every offer shows effective pay after fuel and deductions, your contract red lines are written, your entity and NPI steps are filed in order, and no billable trip is scheduled before written enrollment confirmation and billing setup are in place.

worksheets.title: NEMT Startup Roadmap and Vehicle Fit: Cash, Capital, and the Van Decision
worksheets.purpose: Lock in operating cash, a funded capital tier, and real local demand before buying any vehicle. Then match the van to the client base, the state's entry-style rules, and a written cancellation policy, so the fleet only grows when existing seats are already full.
instructions: Complete the cash reserve and capital tier fields first, because every vehicle decision below depends on how many months of payment lag you can survive.
Do not sign a vehicle note until the monthly burn field shows payment, insurance, fuel, and maintenance totals, with written dealer and insurer quotes attached.
Confirm in writing that your state Medicaid program accepts your chosen entry style before you pick between side-entry and rear-entry vans.
Run overflow prospecting calls and facility visits in the same weeks you shop vehicles, so evidence of demand arrives before the purchase does.
Revisit the expansion trigger every month, and add no vehicle or contract until utilization holds above 70 percent with a current insurance certificate on file.

fields.name: cash_reserve_runway
fields.prompt: Calculate the operating cash reserve you will hold before the first billable trip. List monthly fuel, payroll, insurance, and software costs, then multiply by three to cover the lag between running trips and collecting Medicaid or broker payments.
fields.example: Nemiton sizes the reserve at 90 days of operating cash because Medicaid pays in 30 to 60 days and billing can lag 45 to 90 days [Nemiton — w246jND2Ahw @ 00:06:12]. Example entry: fuel $1,200, insurance $1,440, payroll $3,800, software $160, so $6,600 monthly times three equals a $19,800 reserve before launch.

fields.name: capital_tier
fields.prompt: Name the startup capital tier you are actually funding, the dollar amount committed, and the source of those funds. Explain whether the amount covers vehicle, insurance, credentialing, and reserve, or which item gets deferred until revenue arrives.
fields.example: Tier 1 at $45K to $65K, per Nemiton's three-tier ladder, with Tier 2 at $140K to $190K and Tier 3 above $400K [Nemiton — w246jND2Ahw @ 00:05:17]. Geoff Cole prices an ambulatory single-van launch at $15,000 to $30,000 all in, and $30,000 to $50,000 for wheelchair-accessible [Geoff Cole — dLgmDQavyEU @ 00:05:52]. Funding: personal savings.

fields.name: onramp_choice
fields.prompt: Choose your on-ramp: broker approval with one or two clean cars, private pay first while enrollment is pending, or a facility-first launch. Defend the choice against your state's approval timeline and the cash you can realistically hold today.
fields.example: Private pay first, following Joe Padilla, because Medi-Cal approval takes 5 to 7 months, and MediRoutes notes new owners should not expect 200 broker trips in year one [MediRoutes NEMT Software — g6k_yncRR8o @ 00:22:03]. JT Automations counters that one or two clean cars plus broker approval is enough, since the money is in contracts and volume [JT Automations — dHKhNi-IC-0 @ 00:06:53].

fields.name: overflow_prospecting
fields.prompt: List five dialysis centers, hospitals, or case managers you will ask about transportation overflow this month. Record the contact name, the exact question asked, how they reacted, and the follow-up date you set for each hesitation.
fields.example: Question used: 'Who handles your patient transportation overflow?' JT Automations treats hesitation as an opening, since one case manager or discharge coordinator relationship can bring 100+ rides a month [JT Automations — dHKhNi-IC-0 @ 00:07:46]. Entry: Eastside dialysis, charge nurse hesitated, follow-up Saturday with Padilla-style shift visits [MediRoutes NEMT Software — g6k_yncRR8o @ 00:12:44].

fields.name: vehicle_type_decision
fields.prompt: Decide between an ambulatory sedan, a wheelchair-accessible minivan, or a full-size van. Tie the decision to the share of trip requests in your market, the mobility devices your clients use, and whether multi-loading is required for profitable routes.
fields.example: RouteGenie says a wheelchair minivan can complete up to 90% of contracts, from 63.5% ambulatory plus 30.3% wheelchair requests in Indiana data [RouteGenie — Lh999r_-mi0 @ 00:05:17]. The Wheelchair & Stretcher operator prefers a Ford Transit fitting a stretcher, two wheelchairs, and one ambulatory rider [Wheelchair & Stretcher Transportation Services — svdIU5f-6tA @ 00:00:23].

fields.name: monthly_burn
fields.prompt: Price the full monthly burn on the vehicle before signing any note: down payment, financed payment, commercial insurance, fuel, and maintenance. Convert the total to an annual run cost and state the weekly revenue needed to cover it.
fields.example: NEMT Growth Machine paid $87,900 after taxes for a Ford Transit 350 XL rear-lift van, $6,000 down and about $1,600 monthly [NEMT Growth Machine — nSB43YYfRs0 @ 00:00:00]. Commercial insurance ran about $17,315 a year, roughly $1,440 monthly, pushing fixed cost above $3,000 a month and all-in cost to $43,000 to $45,000 [NEMT Growth Machine — nSB43YYfRs0 @ 00:00:20].

fields.name: entry_style_compliance
fields.prompt: Confirm in writing whether your state Medicaid program and target organizations accept side-entry or rear-entry vans for wheelchair work. Record who confirmed it, the date, and any emergency-exit requirement that could make a purchased van unusable.
fields.example: California denied a rear-entry van without an emergency exit for Medicaid wheelchair work [MJ Business Academy — P_pN6quM3G4 @ 00:11:02]. MJ Business Academy warns against dropping 40, 50, 60,000 on a van certain organizations will not accept [MJ Business Academy — P_pN6quM3G4 @ 00:11:27]. Entry: side entry confirmed by state Medicaid provider services by email, filed with the buyer's order.

fields.name: client_fit_measurement
fields.prompt: Measure the candidate vehicle against your real client base. Note leg extenders, reclining wheelchairs, stretchers, and couples who both ride in wheelchairs, then record whether the floor plan, lift, and securement points handle every case without a second trip.
fields.example: MJ Business Academy flags leg extenders, reclining wheelchairs, and couples who both ride in wheelchairs [MJ Business Academy — ohTDpW0zUS8 @ 00:06:54]. A Mobility Works rep steered Jasmine and Monica from a smaller bench-seat van to the extended cut [MJ Business Academy — P_pN6quM3G4 @ 00:10:25]. AMS Vans stretcher mounts pull out with a 9/16 ratchet [AMS Vans — -DCWDiGaTn0 @ 00:01:20].

fields.name: no_show_policy
fields.prompt: Draft your written no-show and late-cancellation policy. State the notice window, the fee charged inside it, how riders must cancel, the automated reminders you will send, and how you document broker failures to notify you of cancellations.
fields.example: Policy built on a 24-hour notice window with automated trip reminders [RouteGenie — d8ocN3ERJag @ 00:02:26], charging $25 on a $100 trip canceled inside 24 hours [RouteGenie — d8ocN3ERJag @ 00:04:22]. Riders are trained to call the broker directly, and when the broker fails to notify, dispatch calls and gets a note placed on that client account [LearnCargo — MOdO2Zzw1wI @ 00:00:32].

fields.name: expansion_trigger
fields.prompt: Write the expansion trigger you will obey before adding a second vehicle or contract. State the utilization percentage, how you measure it weekly, and the insurance certificate checks that must be current before any new trip is accepted.
fields.example: No expansion until existing vehicles exceed 70% utilization [Nemiton — w246jND2Ahw @ 00:16:25], and RouteGenie warns against taking more contracts than fleet, time and staff can handle [RouteGenie — 3VPGH67xGp8 @ 00:04:29]. A current commercial insurance certificate stays on file, since a personal policy will not cover paid passengers and an expired certificate can block trips [Shantasia_RN — hS8ke40DMr4 @ 00:03:53].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not purchase or finance any vehicle until a 90-day cash reserve is funded, the monthly burn is priced with written quotes, entry style is confirmed in writing with the state, and at least one overflow conversation shows real local demand.

worksheets.title: Brokers, Private Pay, and Facility Contracts: Building a Diversified Trip Book
worksheets.purpose: Measure how much of the business depends on Medicaid brokers, negotiate every broker term in writing, and build a direct pipeline of facility contracts, hospital discharges, and prepaid private-pay riders that carries the margin brokers take away.
instructions: Start with the broker concentration field, because every negotiation and growth decision below depends on how exposed your revenue is to a single broker.
Move every broker conversation about rates, renewals, and disputes to email, and log each exchange in the negotiation field the same day.
Begin re-credentialing the day any broker switch is announced, and track each submission date against the expected 21 to 45 day window.
Schedule in-person facility visits weekly, prepare the after-hours objection response before walking in, and ask for the decision-maker instead of the front desk.
Require prepayment or a signed contract before any private-pay or facility trip runs, and add no more than two new facilities until service holds steady.

fields.name: broker_concentration
fields.prompt: List every broker and direct payer feeding your trips and the percentage of last month's revenue each produced. Flag any single broker above half of revenue and write the specific action that will reduce that dependence within ninety days.
fields.example: Nemiton calls broker concentration the number one hidden risk in NEMT [Nemiton — LjAb-IUYxbM @ 00:13:47]. UMTPG clients who ran 100 percent on one broker lost about $185K and faced a $75K MTM audit claim [United Medical Transportation Providers Group — A2vs7pLblSk @ 00:12:13]. Entry: Modivcare 82%, private pay 18%, action: two facility visits weekly.

fields.name: broker_payment_model
fields.prompt: Identify which payment model your state uses for NEMT: in-house fee-for-service, capitation, managed care organization, or hybrid. Name the brokers operating in your regions, any announced handover dates, and the spread you estimate between state reimbursement and your pay.
fields.example: Nemt University calls in-house fee-for-service administration by the state Medicaid agency the best model [Nemt University — iihLkCuH8NY @ 00:01:12]. Brokers receive the full reimbursement and subpay providers, a 15-35% spread worth $15,000-18,750 yearly on a 3-vehicle fleet [Nemiton — LjAb-IUYxbM @ 00:01:11]. Georgia entry: Verida takes all 5 regions April 1, 2026 [Nemt University — zXw7440bths @ 00:06:26].

fields.name: credentialing_timeline
fields.prompt: Map your broker credentialing timeline step by step. Record the NPI, EIN, and entity documents submitted, the date of each inquiry form, your weekly resubmission schedule, the expected 21 to 45 day window, and the re-credentialing start date after any broker switch.
fields.example: Before partnering with a broker, Nemt University requires an NPI, an EIN, and an LLC or corporation [Nemt University — 0nJ9GYcr744 @ 00:04:31]. About 30 percent of providers fail to re-credential in time when a broker switch is announced, so the clock starts that day [Nemt University — zXw7440bths @ 00:06:26]. Entry: inquiry form resubmitted every Monday until approval.

fields.name: written_negotiation_log
fields.prompt: Keep a written negotiation log for every broker rate, renewal, and dispute. Record the date, the offer received, your counteroffer, and the final written answer, and note every time a broker pushed to move the conversation onto the phone.
fields.example: Every rate, renewal, and dispute exchange goes by email, never phone, to build a paper trail [United Medical Transportation Providers Group — 0Z6CsGngipI @ 00:22:59]. MJ Business Academy says never accept the first offer and keep pushing until you hear final final offer [MJ Business Academy — KSSO5Igfn2Y @ 00:05:52]. Entry: counteroffer sent by email Tuesday.

fields.name: out_of_network_leverage
fields.prompt: Describe when you will work out of network or cherry-pick broker trips instead of accepting the standard rate. State the minimum margin that justifies network participation and the side-door payers, such as county social services, you will approach directly.
fields.example: When a broker reaches out first, UMTPG says you are in the driver's seat: play hard to get over email and work out of network unless the margin is good [United Medical Transportation Providers Group — 0Z6CsGngipI @ 00:06:21]. Motivational Charles reports Vance County Social Services needs providers and pays more than ModivCare [Motivational Charles — BCwbkTt30cY @ 00:03:57].

fields.name: hybrid_mix_target
fields.prompt: Set your target broker-to-private-pay mix for the next six months. Record current monthly revenue, the projected revenue at the target mix, the private-pay rate range you will quote, and the ramp period you are budgeting before results appear.
fields.example: Nemiton models $14,200-18,900 per month at a 70/30 broker/private mix versus $8,700-11,300 at 100% broker, with private pay at $35-85 per trip and a 60-90 day ramp [Nemiton — LjAb-IUYxbM @ 00:08:35]. Diversified operators run 25-40% margins versus 5-15% broker-only [Nemiton — 6nWzJ25nMDg @ 00:00:36]. Target: 70/30 by month six.

fields.name: facility_visit_plan
fields.prompt: Plan your in-person facility visit route for the next four weeks. List nursing homes, rehab centers, dialysis clinics, and hospitals by name, the decision-maker you will ask for, the visit time, and the objection response you will use.
fields.example: In-person visits close 30-50% and referrals 40-60%, while brokers close nothing [Nemiton — 6nWzJ25nMDg @ 00:00:00]. When a facility says it already has a provider, answer: perfect, who does your after-hours work? [Wheelchair & Stretcher Transportation Services — zn8XUaFzOCk @ 00:02:08]. ThatNEMTGirl skips the front desk and pitches executive directors [ThatNEMTGirl — 5gdeSbLFdzk @ 00:32:25].

fields.name: hospital_discharge_pitch
fields.prompt: Build your hospital discharge pitch. Estimate the facility's daily discharge transport spend, the vehicle capability you bring, your average fare and floor, and the audit-exposure argument explaining when Medicaid gets billed and when the hospital pays you directly.
fields.example: Two East Coast hospitals spend $6,000 per weekday on discharge transport and want one provider [United Medical Transportation Providers Group — 3KYWcZTUEuM @ 00:01:21]. Mike Boron averages $230 for 7 miles, floor near $180 [Bambi — bGYVSmlvo90 @ 00:10:53]. Pitch: bill Medicaid when fully covered, otherwise the hospital pays directly and avoids fines [United Medical Transportation Providers Group — HvP2_Kts7vA @ 00:11:30].

fields.name: prepayment_terms
fields.prompt: Write the payment terms you will require from private-pay riders and facilities before any trip runs. Include prepayment rules, net terms offered to facilities, the contract language covering disputed or unauthorized trips, and your fuel-driven rate adjustment clause.
fields.example: MJ Business Academy runs no contract, no trip until payment clears, since otherwise a client may dispute the service, claim it was unauthorized, or cancel [MJ Business Academy — LCV7CgKI3PQ @ 00:04:38]. On pricing, the same operator says it is nothing personal, it is a business, with gas over seven dollars a gallon [MJ Business Academy — LCV7CgKI3PQ @ 00:06:35].

fields.name: growth_pacing
fields.prompt: Set the pace of facility growth you can actually service. Name the first one or two facilities, the vehicle types each account needs, the month you expect pilots to become standing contracts, and the patient feedback you will collect.
fields.example: Nemt Business Life jumped to 20 nursing homes too fast to service, so cap early growth at one or two [Nemt Business Life — UtiLgcZo4dU @ 00:16:55], and remember the patient's opinion drives new contracts [Nemt Business Life — UtiLgcZo4dU @ 00:18:10]. Nemiton says month-two pilots become standing contracts by month four [Nemiton — 6nWzJ25nMDg @ 00:05:10].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign or renew any broker agreement until concentration is measured, every rate exchange sits in an email log, credentialing dates are tracked, and at least one direct facility or prepaid private-pay account is active or scheduled for a pilot.

worksheets.title: Rates, Unit Economics, Dispatch, and Trip Verification: Pricing and Proving Every Trip
worksheets.purpose: Price every trip from your own cost per mile, charge for deadhead and wait time, decline filler work, and run dispatch software that captures signatures, timestamps, and GPS proof, so every billed trip gets paid and survives an audit.
instructions: Calculate cost per mile from last month's actual expenses and miles before filling any rate field, and reprice whenever rates stop covering it.
Write separate base, mileage, wait, and after-hours rates by mobility type instead of one flat rate, and include the price-variation clause on every sheet.
Confirm dead-mile payment with each broker before accepting any trip an hour or more from home base, and log the answer in writing.
Compare at least two dispatch platforms on total fees, broker integration, and multi-load setup before signing, and configure multi-loading payer by payer.
Run the timed audit packet drill monthly, hold any trip missing a verification point, and block any claim where GPS mileage and invoiced mileage disagree.

fields.name: cost_per_mile
fields.prompt: Run your operating cost per mile: total monthly expenses divided by total monthly miles. Show both numbers, the resulting cost per mile, and the lowest per-mile rate you will accept before repricing or declining a trip.
fields.example: Nemt University's formula is total monthly expenses divided by monthly miles, repriced when rates stop covering it [Nemt University — DoH4BLPOrvI @ 00:05:12]. RouteGenie's chart offers $3 to $5 per mile weekdays, $5 to $7 off hours and weekends, and $5 to $10 holidays as starting points [RouteGenie — qceSg9X8F0E @ 00:05:09]. Entry: $9,000 over 4,500 miles equals $2.

fields.name: rate_structure
fields.prompt: Write your rate structure by mobility type: base or load fee, per-mile charge, wait-time fee per 30 minutes, and after-hours, weekend, and holiday premiums. Explain why tiered pricing protects margin better than one flat rate for every trip.
fields.example: Nemt University charges forty dollars just to start the vehicle toward any appointment, noting others may charge 50 to 55 [Nemt University — ZerukPCXB6Q @ 00:06:55]. RouteGenie warns that one rate for all trips hits profitability through losses or thinner margins on after-hours work [RouteGenie — wrfiCapUB9s @ 00:05:47]. Entry: wheelchair base $55, $3 per mile, $20 per 30 minutes wait.

fields.name: deadhead_wait_policy
fields.prompt: Define how you charge for deadhead miles and wait time. State your service radius, the deadhead charge beyond it, which brokers pay dead miles on long trips, and how you price wait time when a broker pays none.
fields.example: With a 25-mile radius, ABC Transport would charge 15 deadhead miles each way on John Smith's trip [RouteGenie — 9j6I5bSKP24 @ 00:02:19]. ThatNEMTGirl confirms the broker pays dead miles before taking trips an hour or more from base [ThatNEMTGirl — govQRXzu6Rg @ 00:04:44]. RouteGenie notes LogistiCare pays no driver wait time at all [RouteGenie — FBWU2kTGLwI @ 00:00:00].

fields.name: revenue_target_math
fields.prompt: Work backward from your monthly revenue target to the completed trips required. State the average reimbursement per trip, the trips needed per week, the weekly floor per vehicle, and the expenses still deducted before any profit remains.
fields.example: Shantasia_RN puts $10,000 monthly at roughly 200 completed trips averaging $50, with payroll, fuel, maintenance, insurance, taxes and software still coming out [Shantasia_RN — 3tRytphhdUU @ 00:01:00]. The stated floor is $500 per vehicle per week, $2,500 across five vehicles [Shantasia_RN — Dr_9wzpyoaE @ 00:00:15]. Entry: 50 trips weekly across two vans.

fields.name: trip_selectivity
fields.prompt: Write your trip selectivity rules. List the broker trips you decline, the minimum fare you accept, the multi-load pairings you build around dialysis and nearby destinations, and the operating hours matched to when brokers actually request trips.
fields.example: ThatNEMTGirl grossed $125,000 in 2024 on one two-wheelchair van with one broker by refusing $35 filler trips [ThatNEMTGirl — govQRXzu6Rg @ 00:01:22], multi-loading nearby dialysis patients [ThatNEMTGirl — govQRXzu6Rg @ 00:01:40], and running 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. weekdays and 6:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Saturdays [ThatNEMTGirl — govQRXzu6Rg @ 00:04:12].

fields.name: rate_sheet_language
fields.prompt: Draft the rate sheet language you send to facilities. Include the off-peak premium framing, the clause stating prices can vary over time, the surcharge trigger tied to fuel, and how you justify rates without cutting below cost.
fields.example: Every MJ Business Academy rate sheet states prices can vary over time, so a surcharge like the $7 to $8 gas spike can be added [MJ Business Academy — aA7hgZoPF_Q @ 00:02:16]. For a 4 a.m. dialysis run, frame the premium as: we are happy to accommodate those early morning hours [Nemt University — DoH4BLPOrvI @ 00:09:42].

fields.name: software_selection
fields.prompt: Compare at least two dispatch platforms before committing. Record the per-vehicle price, setup, messaging, and training fees, broker integrations, multi-load configuration steps, auto-dispatch speed, and whether facility-user logins let partners book their own trips directly in your system.
fields.example: A buyer's notes list RouteGenie at $50 per vehicle per month plus $100 setup, 2.5 cents per text and 5 cents per call, against Bambi's single per-car price [Bambi — CbCgWxHPCxU @ 00:09:38]. RouteGenie integrates with MTM, ModivCare and Access2Care [Nemiton — LjAb-IUYxbM @ 00:16:01]. Bambi requires enabling multi-loading payer by payer [Bambi — dxaejS8Bpis @ 00:00:15].

fields.name: six_point_verification
fields.prompt: Build your six-point trip verification checklist for drivers. For each point, name the in-app evidence captured, such as timestamps, signatures, GPS breadcrumbs, or geofence events, and the rule that holds a trip from billing when any point is missing.
fields.example: Hold any trip lacking service, recipient, provider, date, location, and start and end time [RouteGenie — _mEgB7bAsFE @ 00:01:00]. Drivers capture passenger or facility signatures and mark canceled-at-door or no-show in the MediRoutes app [MediRoutes NEMT Software — nLjDVheWODU @ 00:04:06]. Block claims where GPS breadcrumb mileage does not match invoiced mileage [SwiftAid Transport — YGC_f04Hg3g @ 00:08:34].

fields.name: audit_packet_drill
fields.prompt: Run a timed audit packet drill. Pick three completed trips at random and pull signatures, timestamps, routes, and photos for each. Record the time it took, every missing item, and the fix you will make before the next drill.
fields.example: ZeitRide sets the standard at a full packet of signatures, timestamps, routes, and photos in about 10 minutes instead of a week of scrambling [ZeitRide NEMT Software — ajqkD-2jPd8 @ 00:22:43]. The stakes are real: New York's 2022 audit found $196 million in improper payments and 72% of audited claims non-compliant [SwiftAid Transport — YGC_f04Hg3g @ 00:03:28]. Drill result: 14 minutes.

fields.name: billing_denial_control
fields.prompt: Set your billing and denial controls. Record each broker's submission window, your claim scrubbing step, current denial rate, automated reminder settings that cut no-shows, and the incoming broker transitions you must credential with before day one.
fields.example: Metro Medical Transport cut denials from 23% to 6% in six months with automated claim scrubbing and broker API integration, recovering $200,000 a month [SwiftAid Transport — YGC_f04Hg3g @ 00:37:06]. RouteGenie reminder calls plus trip tracking can reduce no-shows up to 50% [RouteGenie — j__fVq5xHLo @ 00:01:37]. Montana Medicaid trips require Modivcare enrollment before transition [RouteGenie — GWBpqyUYyjE @ 00:06:24].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not bill a single trip until cost per mile is calculated, tiered rates and the price-variation clause are written, dispatch software captures all six verification points, and a timed audit packet drill has been completed in under 15 minutes.
